title: I AM: who Jesus says He is
opening_question: At the burning bush God gave Moses His name: I AM THAT I AM. In the Gospel of John, Jesus says I am again and again: the bread of life, the light of the world, the door, the good shepherd, the resurrection and the life, the way, the truth and the life, the true vine. What does He claim each time, and why did some take up stones? Each step asks what He said and what it means for me.

steps.intro: Background first: before Jesus said I am in John, God gave Moses His name at the burning bush (Exodus 3).
steps.question: What did Moses ask God at the bush, and what name did God give him?
steps.apply: Do I know God by His name, or only as an idea?

facts.text: Moses asked what to say when the people would ask "What is his name?"
God answered: "I AM THAT I AM", and "I AM hath sent me unto you".
"I AM" comes from hayah. Strong's: "to exist".
The name the KJV prints as "The LORD" in the next verse is YHWH. Strong's: "From H1961", "self Existent or eternal". God adds: "this is my name for ever".

steps.question: What did the people ask Jesus for, and what did He say about the true bread from heaven?
steps.apply: What am I hungry for, and do I come to Him to be filled?

facts.text: Moses gave manna, but Jesus said: "my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven".
"I am" is ego eimi. Ego, Strong's: "only expressed when emphatic"; eimi: "I exist".
"Your fathers did eat manna in the wilderness, and are dead." His bread is different: "if any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever".
He said what the bread is: "my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world".

steps.question: What did Jesus say about Himself in John 8:12, and what did He do for the man born blind?
steps.apply: Where am I still walking in darkness when I could follow the light?

facts.text: "he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life".
"light" is phos. Strong's: "luminousness".
The disciples asked "who did sin". Jesus answered: "that the works of God should be made manifest in him".
Right after "I am the light of the world", He gave a blind man his sight: "He went his way therefore, and washed, and came seeing".

steps.question: What did Jesus say about Abraham, and why did the people take up stones to cast at Him?
steps.apply: Is Jesus to me only a good teacher, or the One who always is?

facts.text: He did not say I was. He said "Before Abraham was, I am". "was" is ginomai, Strong's: "to become"; "am" is eimi, "I exist". Abraham came to be; He is.
"Then took they up stones to cast at him". The law said: "he that blasphemeth the name of the LORD, he shall surely be put to death". They understood what He claimed.
In "I am he" the KJV prints "he" in italics: the translators added it. The Greek has only ego eimi, I am.

steps.question: What did Jesus call Himself in John 10:7-9, and what does the thief come to do?
steps.apply: Am I trying to come to God some other way than through Him?

facts.text: "by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture".
"door" is thura. Strong's: "a portal or entrance".
The thief comes "to steal, and to kill, and to destroy". He came "that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly".

steps.question: What does the good shepherd do that the hireling does not?
steps.apply: Do I trust Him to lead me, and do I let Him know me?

facts.text: "the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep". The hireling "seeth the wolf coming, and leaveth the sheep, and fleeth".
"good" is kalos. Strong's: "valuable or virtuous".
David wrote "The LORD is my shepherd". Jesus says "I am the good shepherd".
He knows His own: "I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep", "and am known of mine".

steps.question: What did Martha believe about the last day, and what did Jesus tell her He is?
steps.apply: Jesus asks me what He asked Martha. Do I believe this?

facts.text: Martha said "I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day". Jesus answered with Himself: "I am the resurrection, and the life".
"resurrection" is anastasis. Strong's: "a standing up again".
He asked her: "Believest thou this?" She answered: "Yea, Lord: I believe that thou art the Christ, the Son of God".

steps.question: What did Thomas ask, and what did Jesus answer?
steps.apply: Am I still looking for a way to God, or have I come to the Way?

facts.text: Thomas asked "how can we know the way?" Jesus did not point to a way. He said "I am the way".
"way" is hodos, Strong's: "a road". "truth" is aletheia.
"no man cometh unto the Father, but by me".

steps.question: What does the Father do with the branches, and what does Jesus say we can do without Him?
steps.apply: What does it look like for me to abide in Him, day by day?

facts.text: "I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman." "true" is alethinos, Strong's: "truthful".
"abide" is meno. Strong's: "to stay".
"without me ye can do nothing".
The fruit is for the Father: "Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit".

steps.intro: Closing: every I am in John points back to the name God gave at the burning bush.
steps.question: What happened when Jesus said "I am he" in the garden, and how does He name Himself at the end of the Bible?
steps.apply: If He is the first and the last, what in my life do I still need to hand over to Him?

facts.text: Judas came with "a band of men and officers", "with lanterns and torches and weapons".
When He said "I am he", "they went backward, and fell to the ground". Here too the KJV prints "he" in italics.
He gave Himself up and asked them to let His disciples go: "if therefore ye seek me, let these go their way".
At the end of the Bible He says: "I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last".

remember.text: "I am the light of the world"
"I am the resurrection, and the life"
"I am the way, the truth, and the life"
"I am the vine, ye are the branches"
